_comment: Filled in as things are actually implemented, not ahead of reality — see docs/scenarios/ for what's actually built. All nodes/connections here are always shown - no teaching-progression scenario filter anymore.

components.name: k6 (load test)
components.description: Traffic generator started from the control panel - not part of the deployed stack, only exists while a run is active

details.purpose: One-off container per run (see the traffic panel); hits the same external entry point (nginx) real clients would

components.name: nginx
components.description: External entry point for LinkApi and RedirectApi - the only reason either can have more than one replica

details.purpose: Reverse proxy in front of link-api/redirect-api; re-resolves their service name against Docker's embedded DNS on a short TTL so it picks up replicas added/removed via Scale without a config reload. Also internally fans out gRPC calls (messaging-mode=grpc) to shortener-service/traffic-service on ports 9090/9091 - not published to the host, same resolve-based upstream pattern as its HTTP reverse-proxying. ReportingService has no gRPC endpoint to fan out to (see the redirect-api → nginx edge's own notes)

components.name: Frontend App
components.description: Demo UI — register/login, create a short link, visit it

details.purpose: The only thing an actual person interacts with in this whole stack

components.name: AuthApi
components.description: Registration / login, issues a JWT access token + rotating refresh token

details.purpose: Owns users_db (the only writer to it, and the only one that migrates it); refresh tokens are stored there too, one row per issued token, rotated (old one revoked) on every refresh

components.name: LinkApi
components.description: Creates short links (hash generated here), reads them back through a cache

details.purpose: POST /links generates the hash, optionally attaches userId from a Bearer token (no [Authorize] — anonymous still works), and publishes it; GET /links/{hash} is a cached read against links_db; GET /links (paginated) lists a user's own links

components.name: RedirectApi
components.description: Resolves a short link, issues a 302, bumps the click counter, and records the click

details.purpose: Cache-first read of links_db (same data LinkApi writes); 404 on unknown hash; increments a Redis click counter (hot path, doesn't wait on Postgres) and publishes ClickTrackedEvent right before redirecting

components.name: RabbitMQ
components.description: Durable queue between the two APIs and their workers

details.purpose: Decouples each API's synchronous response from the actual Postgres/Mongo writes it triggers
details.topology: topic exchange "events"; queue "shortener-service.link-created" bound to routing key "link.created"; ClickTracked events fan out to three independent queues bound to "click.tracked" - "shortener-service.click-tracked" (bumps the display click count), "traffic-service.click-tracked" (the durable click record + Mongo metadata), and "reporting-service.click-tracked" (the CQRS read model in ClickHouse) - all declared by the app itself, not a static definitions.json

links.config: sandbox/infra/rabbitmq/definitions.json (unused placeholder, see its own comment)

components.name: ShortenerService
components.description: Consumes LinkCreatedEvent (persists the link) and ClickTrackedEvent (bumps its click count)

details.purpose: Owns links_db (the only writer, and the only one that migrates it); both consumers are redelivery-safe - LinkCreated skips if the hash is already stored, ClickTracked just re-increments (an approximate display counter, not the audit trail - that's TrafficService's Clicks table)

components.name: TrafficService
components.description: Consumes ClickTrackedEvent, persists the click record and its enriched metadata

details.purpose: Owns clicks_db (the only writer, and the only one that migrates it) - Postgres Clicks is the exactly-once audit trail (skips if the event's Id is already stored); also parses the User-Agent and resolves geo-IP, then upserts a ClickMeta document into MongoDB, independently idempotent from the Postgres write

components.name: PgCat
components.description: Connection pooler in front of Postgres - every service talks to pgcat, never to postgres directly

details.purpose: One pool per physical database (users_db/links_db/clicks_db), each backed by the same 3 physical servers (primary + 2 replicas); query_parser_read_write_splitting auto-routes plain SELECTs across all 3 and everything else (writes, DDL, transactions) to the primary only - no app-side read/write split needed

components.name: Redis (master)
components.description: Cache of hash → link, plus the atomic per-link click counter - the actual data-plane target once Sentinel discovery has picked it out

details.purpose: Cache-aside for links (read-through on miss, shared key format between LinkApi and RedirectApi) and an INCR-based click counter; link-api/redirect-api never dial this hostname directly - their Sentinel-aware connection string talks to redis-sentinel-1/2/3 first, which report back whichever node is currently master

components.name: Redis Replica 1
components.description: Async replica of redis-master - not written to directly by the app, only ever a promotion target

details.purpose: Kept current via Redis's own async replication off redis-master; the three Sentinels promote one of the two replicas to master if redis-master stops responding

components.name: Redis Replica 2
components.description: Async replica of redis-master - not written to directly by the app, only ever a promotion target

details.purpose: Kept current via Redis's own async replication off redis-master; the three Sentinels promote one of the two replicas to master if redis-master stops responding

components.name: Redis Sentinel 1
components.description: Watches redis-master/replica1/replica2 and votes with the other two Sentinels on failover (quorum 2 of 3)

details.purpose: link-api/redirect-api's Redis client asks all three Sentinels who the current master is before ever touching cache data - this is what makes redis-master swappable on failover without an app restart or config change

components.name: Redis Sentinel 2
components.description: Watches redis-master/replica1/replica2 and votes with the other two Sentinels on failover (quorum 2 of 3)

details.purpose: link-api/redirect-api's Redis client asks all three Sentinels who the current master is before ever touching cache data - this is what makes redis-master swappable on failover without an app restart or config change

components.name: Redis Sentinel 3
components.description: Watches redis-master/replica1/replica2 and votes with the other two Sentinels on failover (quorum 2 of 3)

details.purpose: link-api/redirect-api's Redis client asks all three Sentinels who the current master is before ever touching cache data - this is what makes redis-master swappable on failover without an app restart or config change

components.name: Mongo 1
components.description: One member of a 3-node MongoDB replica set (rs0) - holds clicks_meta_db, the click metadata TrafficService enriches with parsed browser/OS/device + geo

details.purpose: No fixed primary by container identity, unlike Postgres - the replica set itself elects a primary among mongo1/2/3, and the driver (seeded with all three) auto-discovers whichever one it currently is

components.name: Mongo 2
components.description: One member of a 3-node MongoDB replica set (rs0) - holds clicks_meta_db, the click metadata TrafficService enriches with parsed browser/OS/device + geo

details.purpose: No fixed primary by container identity, unlike Postgres - the replica set itself elects a primary among mongo1/2/3, and the driver (seeded with all three) auto-discovers whichever one it currently is

components.name: Mongo 3
components.description: One member of a 3-node MongoDB replica set (rs0) - holds clicks_meta_db, the click metadata TrafficService enriches with parsed browser/OS/device + geo

details.purpose: No fixed primary by container identity, unlike Postgres - the replica set itself elects a primary among mongo1/2/3, and the driver (seeded with all three) auto-discovers whichever one it currently is

components.name: users_db
components.description: Own physical database, not just a schema — real isolation from links_db/clicks_db

details.purpose: Users(id, name, email, passwordHash, sault) + RefreshTokens(id, userId, tokenHash, expiresAt, revokedAt?)

components.name: links_db
components.description: Own physical database — target design shards this one (scenario 4)

details.purpose: Links(hash PK, originalLink, shortenLink, createdAt, userId?, clickCount)

components.name: clicks_db
components.description: Own physical database

details.purpose: Clicks(id, clickedAt, inboundLink, outboundLink, hash)

components.name: Postgres Replica 1
components.description: Streaming (physical) replica of the whole cluster - bootstraps via pg_basebackup, then runs as an ordinary hot standby

details.purpose: Read-only copy of users_db/links_db/clicks_db together (Postgres replicates the whole cluster, not per-database) kept current via WAL streaming from postgres; pgcat load-balances SELECT-only queries across this, postgres-replica2, and the primary

components.name: Postgres Replica 2
components.description: Streaming (physical) replica of the whole cluster - bootstraps via pg_basebackup, then runs as an ordinary hot standby

details.purpose: Read-only copy of users_db/links_db/clicks_db together (Postgres replicates the whole cluster, not per-database) kept current via WAL streaming from postgres; pgcat load-balances SELECT-only queries across this, postgres-replica1, and the primary

components.name: ReportingService
components.description: CQRS read side: a third, independent consumer of ClickTrackedEvent - builds its own denormalized read model in ClickHouse, straight from the raw event, never from traffic-service's own Postgres/Mongo writes

details.purpose: Owns reports_db in ClickHouse (the only writer) - parses the same raw UserAgent/geo-IP as traffic-service does independently, then does one bulk insert per consumed batch; single-row inserts are a real ClickHouse anti-pattern this service specifically avoids

components.name: ReportingApi
components.description: Read-only query side of the CQRS split - queries ClickHouse directly for the frontend's per-link stats panel, never touches the write path

details.purpose: GET /reports/{hash}/summary aggregates total clicks plus by-day/country/device/browser breakdowns via raw parameterized SQL against ClickHouse - no ORM, since this is the one place meant to show what a columnar OLAP query actually looks like

components.name: ClickHouse
components.description: Columnar OLAP store holding reports_db.clicks - a third, independent sink for the same click data already living in Postgres (clicks_db) and Mongo (clicks_meta_db), each teaching a different "right tool for the job" lesson

details.purpose: clicks is a ReplacingMergeTree table ordered by (hash, id) - a redelivered event eventually collapses to one row during a background merge instead of reporting-service needing to query first (ClickHouse is specifically bad at point lookups), so a query right after a redelivery can briefly still double-count until the next merge runs

connections.notes: Only active in messaging-mode=grpc. Internal port 9090, not published to the host - same `resolve`-based upstream pattern nginx already uses for link-api/redirect-api, so scaling shortener-service's replica count stays transport-agnostic.

connections.label: Fan out gRPC calls across replicas
connections.notes: Only active in messaging-mode=grpc. Internal port 9091, not published to the host.

connections.label: Cache read-through on GET
connections.format: link:{hash} → JSON
connections.notes: Connects via Sentinel discovery (redis-sentinel-1/2/3) - the client asks them who's current master and reconnects automatically on failover, no code involved.

connections.label: Read on cache miss
connections.format: read-only from this service — ShortenerService owns writes/migrations

connections.label: Publish LinkCreatedEvent
connections.format: { hash, originalLink, shortenLink, createdAt, userId? } → JSON, routing key "link.created"
connections.notes: Falls back to a local SQLite queue if the broker is unreachable; retried every 30s. Only active in messaging-mode=rabbitmq (the default) - see the alternative gRPC edge below.

connections.label: Dispatch LinkCreatedEvent (sync)
connections.format: PublishRequest { messageId, topic: "link.created", payload } - payload is the same JSON the RabbitMQ publish would send
connections.notes: Only active in messaging-mode=grpc (control-api's messaging-mode toggle, on the rabbitmq node) - the alternative to the AMQP edge above. CreateLink's HTTP response doesn't return until ShortenerService has actually persisted the row; a failed call fails the request (502/503) instead of falling back to a queue - see SyncGrpcDispatcher's own comment for why that's deliberate.

connections.label: Consume LinkCreatedEvent + ClickTrackedEvent
connections.notes: Two independent queues, both bound here - LinkCreated persists the link, ClickTracked (fanned out alongside traffic-service below) just bumps its click count. Drawn as one connection since both land on this same node pair; see each queue's own consumer for the distinct handling.

connections.label: Persist the link / increment its click count
connections.format: the only writer for links_db; click count is an approximate display counter, not the audit trail - see traffic-service's own Clicks table for that

connections.label: Cache lookup + increment click counter
connections.format: link:{hash} → JSON (cache read) and link:{hash}:clicks → INCR (counter), both on every visit
connections.notes: Connects via Sentinel discovery (redis-sentinel-1/2/3) - the client asks them who's current master and reconnects automatically on failover, no code involved. The counter increment is a hot-path fire-and-forget; the durable "my links" click count is synced separately, asynchronously, off ClickTrackedEvent via ShortenerService.

connections.label: Read on cache miss
connections.format: read-only from this service — ShortenerService owns writes/migrations

connections.label: Publish ClickTrackedEvent
connections.format: { id, hash, inboundLink, outboundLink, clickedAt, userAgent, referrer, ipAddress } → JSON, routing key "click.tracked"
connections.notes: Published right before the 302 response; falls back to the same SQLite-queue pattern as LinkApi if the broker is unreachable. A 404 never publishes anything. Only active in messaging-mode=rabbitmq (the default) - see the alternative gRPC edge below.

connections.label: Dispatch ClickTrackedEvent (sync)
connections.format: PublishRequest { messageId, topic: "click.tracked", payload }
connections.notes: Only active in messaging-mode=grpc - the alternative to the AMQP edge above. Targets TrafficService only - nothing is ever published to RabbitMQ in this mode, so the other two fan-out consumers of click.tracked (ShortenerService's click-count bump, ReportingService's ClickHouse write) never receive the event either; both go stale while gRPC mode is active, a known asymmetry of point-to-point RPC vs. pub/sub fan-out for this v1. The redirect itself doesn't return until TrafficService has persisted the click - the hottest path in the whole system becomes coupled to a downstream analytics write's availability, which is the entire point of this mode.

connections.label: Consume ClickTrackedEvent (CQRS fan-out)
connections.notes: A third, independent queue bound to the same click.tracked routing key traffic-service already consumes - redirect-api's publish side is unchanged; this is fan-out, not a chain.

connections.label: Bulk insert click facts
connections.format: one InsertBinaryAsync call per consumed batch - never per row
